description: the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 88's §122 surcharge was zeroed on the witness's exemplar-line flags entry_is_line_a/entry_is_line_b rather than on the 9903.03.03 exclusion list and the §232-covered aluminum/steel/copper carve-out its own proof atoms cite, suppressing the surcharge on §301-member lines of every origin, and the other authority components were likewise gated on exemplar identity rather than list membership.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 84; this file is byte-identical in normalized diff to index 84 (same 'effective_from:' spelling). Same caveats as index 84.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere "generalization" (the commit subject is "generalize generated component surfaces") but the diff changes encoded meaning, not just names: `section_122_component_rate` version[1] stops zeroing the surcharge on the witness's exemplar-identity flags and is re-grounded on `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered`, the two exception classes its own proof atoms cite (9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list; "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"). The pre-fix condition was demonstrably untraceable: in the same module `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b` simultaneously carry China-§301 list-1 and 2024-action membership (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`), so the §122 exclusion branch was in fact grounded on §301 list / 9903.01.33 metals-proxy membership rather than on the §122 exclusion list — the PR's "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins," and the resolved 9903.01.33 text confirms the exclusion is an article-class list ("of any country"), not a line-identity test. The same re-grounding is applied to the §232 aluminum, China-301, Brazil-301 and forced-labor-301 branches, and the PR records 18 witness-slice cells whose values changed because "the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part," so this is a meaning change, not provenance bookkeeping. Untraceable_branch is the right kind (a branch condition with no basis in the cited provision, re-grounded by the fix); wrong_entity_or_scope is the only serious competitor and it fits worse because entity, period and program scope are untouched.
triage.verifier_notes: Corroboration: in the pre file `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` has `formula: entry_is_line_a` and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` has `formula: entry_is_line_b`, while `china_section_301_component_rate` uses the same two flags for list-1 and 2024-action membership — one boolean carrying two different memberships is the concrete mechanism of the "unlawful suppression." Scope caveats for the reviewer: (1) this file is a generator-emitted composition ("generator b1.6-schedule-compositions-2" → "-3", "hand edits prohibited"), so the defect lives in tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py and was replicated across all 100 chapter modules; ch88 is one instance, not an independent defect. (2) Not every hunk in this diff is a correction: the `section_201_component_rate` swap (`if entry_is_line_e: 0 else: 0` → `if entry_is_section_201_cspv: 0 else: 0`) is value-neutral, and the new `section_232_steel_component_rate` + its stack term is added coverage the module never claimed (the PR itself says "a Section 232 steel component the witness never had"), which is not a defect — if the corpus wants one defect per commit-module, the §122/§301/§232-aluminum/Brazil/forced-labor re-grounding is the defect and the steel component is a separate enhancement. (3) The steel component shipped here with malformed double-nested `metadata: proof: proof: atoms:`, repaired in a follow-up per the PR issue comment ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical `metadata.proof.atoms`"); ignore that for classification. (4) Post-fix, `entry_is_line_d` survives (beer/§338, "because no membership module exists") and Brazil/forced-labor membership inputs default FALSE, so the decoupling is deliberately partial.
